title: surprise-meter
gist: A small world model trained from scratch on a laptop, on nothing but next-frame pixels, and tested the way psychophysics tests a person: a lawful clip against an impossible twin, with an ideal observer as the yardstick. That yardstick caught a probe that seemed to see more than the model and was only drawing the ball too bright.
summary: Lets anyone watch a world model guess each frame in the browser, break its physics with a finger, and see how surprised it is.

hero_image.alt: A ball goes behind a slab in a small noisy frame, and an outline of where the model's state places the hidden ball is drawn over it.

site.blurb: A world model trained on next-frame pixels, tested with matched lawful and impossible clips against an ideal observer. A probe of its state seemed to keep a hidden ball in view more than twice as long as the model did, until on a frame where both clips share one state it beat the observer that knows the answer, 0.78 against 0.66. It was painting the ball 1.2 to 1.9 times too bright.
